To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the central difference scheme used in the LES of Beaudan et al. is not suitable for LES in the near wake region, and that higher order upwind-biassed schemes are more suitable for LES in complex geometry.
the energy-conservative central difference scheme is not suitable for large-eddy simulations of flows with strong shear layers and/or strong vorticity gradients.

(1) the second-order central difference spatial discretization scheme is suitable for the LES of the flow past a circular-cylinder at Re = 3.9x10 3, and (2) a second-order upwind scheme with an appropriate limiter is not a suitable choice for the LES of this flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical methods and algorithms for the simulation of complex turbulent flow phenomena.
the numerical aspects of LES, and we have not attempted a detailed study of the physical mechanisms responsible for drag and lift reduction in the wake region.
the development of a numerical method for large-eddy simulations of turbulent flows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of higher-order upwinding schemes in LES of wall-bounded turbulent flow is not recommended.
the use of higher-order upwinding is not recommended for LES of flows with complex geometry, especially if the flow is characterized by a strong mean shear.

, for LES of complex turbulent flows at high Reynolds numbers, a second-order upwind scheme is not necessarily superior to a second-order central difference (CD) scheme, but a fourth-order upwind scheme (or a fifth-order CD scheme) is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the second-order central difference method performs as well as the fourth- and sixth-order upwind-biases methods for this case.
higher-order upwind-biases schemes are more appropriate for LES than central difference schemes.
the central scheme is more suitable for LES of complex flows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central difference scheme performs better than the upwind schemes for the flow considered.
upwind-biassed schemes can be used for LES of complex flows provided that a sufficient number of grid points are employed in the vicinity of the flow features.
the energy-conservative central difference scheme is adequate for LES in the absence of strong shock waves.
